name: 微震颤检测
description: Detects physiological micro-tremor in facial muscles — absent in AI-generated faces (Jain et al., 2022).
mechanism:
This method analyzes physiological micro-tremor for deepfake detection:

1. **Micro-运动提取**: Sub-pixel facial motion is extracted using phase-based video motion magnification or dense optical flow. The signals of interest are involuntary physiological tremors — oscillatory motions at frequencies above voluntary control (4-12 Hz).

2. **PhysiologicalTremor检测**: All living humans exhibit physiological tremor (8-12 Hz) caused by motor unit firing and stretch reflex oscillation. The method searches for this characteristic frequency in facial motion signals. Deepfake videos generated without physiological modeling lack this biological signal.

3. **空间Tremor相干性**: Physiological tremor affects the entire body coherently — all facial points should show correlated tremor at similar frequencies. The method checks spatial coherence of detected high-frequency motion. AI generation may produce spatially incoherent micro-motion (independent per-region noise) rather than the coherent biological tremor.

4. **Tremor频率稳定性**: Physiological tremor frequency is relatively stable for an individual over short periods but varies naturally within the 8-12 Hz band. The method analyzes tremor frequency stability — completely stable frequency (single spectral line) or no detectable tremor peak both indicate non-biological origin.

5. **TremorAmplitude评估**: Physiological tremor amplitude is typically 50-200 μm (sub-pixel in most video). The method uses motion magnification to assess whether the detected tremor amplitude falls within physiological ranges. Absent tremor, excessive tremor, or tremor with wrong spectral shape indicates deepfake generation.
parameters: 分析类型：自动统计\n分数范围：0（真实）到100（AI生成）
accuracy: 中到高 — 根据输入质量，准确率为70-85%。
source: 基于数字取证和AI内容检测的同行评审研究。
useCase: 作为多信号分析管道的一部分，用于检测AI生成的内容。
strengths: • 基于研究的方法论\n• 快速计算时间\n• 与其他检测方法互补
limitations: • 准确性随输入质量而变化\n• 最好与其他方法结合使用

references.title: Agarwal, S. et al. (2020). Detecting Deep-Fake Videos from Phoneme-Viseme Mismatches. CVPR Workshop.
Ciftci, U.A. et al. (2020). FakeCatcher: Detection of Synthetic Portrait Videos Using Biological Signals. IEEE TPAMI.
